name: Casa Baglioni Milan
positioning: Townhouse hotel in Milan's Brera district, designed around the art and design of 1960s Milan
best_for: Travelers drawn to Milanese art and midcentury Italian design
Food lovers who want chef Claudio Sadler's Milanese cooking under the same roof

facts.text: Casa Baglioni Milan is in the Brera district of Milan.
The hotel's design is inspired by the art and design of 1960s Milan, mixing traditional Italian style with modern innovation.
Room decor includes lighting by Panzeri, wallpaper by Rubelli, fabrics by Dedar and fittings by Zucchetti.
The Deluxe Suite is a tribute to Italian craftsmanship and Gio Ponti's Milan.
The Deluxe Suite comes with Acqua di Parma bathroom amenities.
Rooms are done in chestnut wood with midcentury sofas and armchairs.
The lobby's neon-strip chandelier nods to Lucio Fontana-designed light fittings at the Museo del Novecento.
Claudio Sadler's tasting menu includes Milanese dishes such as risotto Milanese, veal and local cheese.
The fitness center is equipped with Technogym machines.
The hotel offers a tour of the Brera district that includes the Pinacoteca di Brera.
Experiences offered include a private Lake Como trip from Milan.

highlights.text: Chef Claudio Sadler's cooking at the hotel reinvents regional Milanese traditions.
The hotel occupies a townhouse built in the 1910s that once belonged to fashion designer Philipp Plein.
The rooftop serves drinks and aperitivo with panoramic views of Milan.
The suites feature inlaid wood floors and geometric shapes and colors typical of the Spatialist avant-garde movement.
The hotel's Wine Cellar can be booked for private tastings.

considerations.text: Balconies with views of the Brera district come with some rooms, not all.
Pets are welcome only if small or medium-sized, and a supplement is charged per stay.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing that reflects the hotel's luxury positioning.
